05 · ATMOSFAIRUX/UI · Web Redesign · Climate Communication

Making climate action easier to navigate.

A website redesign exploring a clearer journey from understanding personal emissions to discovering ways to take climate action.

Role
UX/UI Designer
Project
Academic redesign project
Focus
Climate communication
Output
Website redesign

The challenge

Making climate information easier to act on.

The project explored how atmosfair content could fit into a flight-booking journey. The team tested the placement of offset options, sustainability messaging on a landing page and different donation formats at checkout. Alongside this work, the website redesign explores a more visible route into climate information and action.

Testing & insights

What we learned along the way.

The presentation records three test scenarios. These observations describe behaviour within those test concepts; they are not measured results for the final website.

01

Context influenced the choice

In Test 2, the presentation reports that 63.2% selected the Eco option after the atmosfair-focused landing page, compared with 48.1% after the standard page.

02

Exploration and continuation differed

In Test 1, 70% opened the offset option. Of those who opened it, 75% continued with the offset process.

03

Donation format mattered

Scenario 3 found greater willingness to donate when the donation element was more noticeable and amounts were predetermined.

Project presentation · Test 2, pp. 9–10 · Test 1, pp. 18–19 · Scenario 3, pp. 17, 20, 22

Iteration

Turning feedback into changes.

The documented checkout variants make the design alternatives visible: Version 2 uses a custom donation field beside the payment form; Version 3 gives donation a larger area with preset amounts and a custom option. The reported findings favoured the more noticeable, predetermined donation approach.

Final design

Bringing the experience together.

The final redesign brings the project direction into one continuous website experience, creating a clearer path through climate information, projects and opportunities for action.

What changed through testing.

The clearest documented design decisions concern the tested booking concepts.

01

Make the choice visible

The checkout exploration moved from a smaller custom-amount panel to a prominent donation area. The presentation identifies visibility as a factor in willingness to donate.

02

Offer a starting amount

The preset-amount variant gives people concrete choices while retaining a custom option. The presentation identifies predetermined amounts as the strongest direction in Scenario 3.

Reflection

What I took from it.

This project showed me how much the way a choice is presented can matter. Testing different versions helped me look beyond what seemed visually clear to me and pay more attention to how people understood the options in front of them.
